subject: Urgent: regional LB backpressure -> 5xx/429 surge impacting Stratus checkout
messages:
From: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@stratusretail.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: sre@stratusretail.com
Date: 2026-11-30T16:12:00+00:00
Subject: High 503/429 rate during EU evening peak - checkout failing

Hi support,

We started seeing a sudden uptick in 503/504 and 429s hitting our checkout flows in eu-west-1 around 15:40 UTC. This coincides with a flash promotion surge (attached heatmap). Customers are seeing timeouts and the frontend is returning 502/503. Our retries appear to be amplifying the load.

Symptoms summary:
- LB returning 502/503/504; backend proxy pool showing 5xx spikes.
- Inference API returning 429s mid-stream; some token generation aborts.
- Retry middleware on checkout is reissuing requests rapidly -> visible retry storms.
- KV-cache miss rate jumped 8x.

Impacted endpoints: /checkout, /cart/checkout/express
Estimated failed checkout rate: ~18% during 15:40-16:05 UTC window.

Attached: support_log_snippet.txt, screenshot-429-1200x800.png, traffic-heatmap-nov30.csv

Please advise immediate mitigations: can you route traffic away from eu-west or spike capacity? We need an ops contact and ETA.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Head of Ops, Stratus Retail
From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@stratusretail.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T16:19:00+00:00
Subject: Re: High 503/429 rate during EU evening peak - checkout failing

Evelyn — thanks for the detailed notes and attachments.

Immediate actions:
- I've triggered our emergency routing policy to divert new requests from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 for Stratus traffic only (canary 10% -> 50%).
- Asking infra to provision burst Dedicated capacity in eu region (ETA 25m).
- SREs: please paste logs and top error traces in the shared Drive link.

Hannah / Marissa / Sean: can one of you pair with Stratus SREs on a rolling mitigation? We need to stop retry amplification and identify whether the 429s are caused by internal rate limits or backend slowdowns.

I'll keep Evelyn and the Stratus team updated every 15 minutes.

-Markus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@stratusretail.com>, sre@stratusretail.com
Date: 2026-11-30T16:26:00+00:00
Subject: Re: High 503/429 rate during EU evening peak - checkout failing

On Tue, 30 Nov 2026 at 16:19, markus.klein@redwood.com wrote:
> I've triggered our emergency routing policy to divert new requests from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 for Stratus traffic only (canary 10% -> 50%).

Pairing notes from SRE triage (summary):
- Initial root cause hypothesis: regional LB under backpressure from sudden traffic spike; backend inference nodes hit CPU/GPU contention -> increased tail latency -> LB returning 502/504.
- Secondary: internal short-window throttles are returning 429s for streaming token generation when KV cache misses are high.
- Retry middleware in Stratus frontend is configured with aggressive exponential backoff disabled; it is retrying on 5xx and 429 synchronously, amplifying load.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Disabled Stratus client-side retry plugin for checkout routes (temp flag via feature gate).
- Increased per-model concurrency limits on the affected inference pool by 30% and added a short token-rate limiter to smooth bursts.
- Enabled prefix caching for common checkout prompts to reduce token generation calls.

Request to Product/Runtime: we need a temporary automatic fallback to a smaller, quantized model for streams that are >1s to first token to reduce resource pressure. Can we enable a targeted fallback for Stratus in eu?

-Hannah
Senior SRE
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@stratusretail.com>, sre@stratusretail.com
Date: 2026-11-30T16:43:00+00:00
Subject: Re: High 503/429 rate during EU evening peak - checkout failing

Status update for Stratus:
- Traffic diversion to eu-central progressed to 60% after 20m; error rate in eu-west falling but still elevated on tail latency (p95-p99).
- After disabling retries and increasing concurrency limits, the 429 rate from inference decreased ~70% within 12 minutes.
- KV-cache hit rate improved when prefix caching enabled; checkout success rate rose from 82% -> 92% for diverted traffic.

Actions next 2 hours:
- Run a capacity probe (non-customer traffic) to validate new pool headroom.
- Postmortem owner: sean_gallagher (collect logs, config diffs, timeline).
- Recommend post-incident change: auto-rewrite aggressive client retry configs on customer SDKs when we detect LB 5xx spikes.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success Ops
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, Evelyn Price <evelyn.price@stratusretail.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:03:00+00:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: Stratus EU flash sale surge (Nov 30)

Hi all,

Final summary and next steps:
- Root cause: regional LB backpressure + backend inference node tail latency due to simultaneous burst of streaming requests with high KV-cache miss rate. This caused cascading 502/504 at proxy tier and internal 429s.
- Mitigations applied: targeted traffic diversion, temporary disabling of aggressive client retries, increased concurrency on affected inference pool, prefix caching, and temporary token-rate smoothing.
- Impact window: 2026-11-30T15:40:00Z - 2026-11-30T16:20:00Z; peak failed checkout rate ~18%.

Follow-ups (owners):
- SRE (sean_gallagher): full timeline + logs upload to Drive + incident page (due EOD 2026-12-02).
- Runtime team (grace_oconnor): evaluate automatic model fallback policy for high-latency streams (proposal due 2026-12-07).
- DX/SDK (marissa_cole): recommend safe retry defaults & feature flag to opt-out of aggressive retries (proposal due 2026-12-05).

Evelyn: thank you for rapid coordination; we'll schedule a 30-min retrospective with Stratus leadership tomorrow to review the SLA credit and long-term mitigations.

-sean
Senior Incident Manager
Redwood Inference
